messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT triggered: high runtime queue latency on us-west-2-serving (p95 queue time > 3s) — Pager: alice. Priority: P1

alice: acked. grabbing telemetry now. seeing spike in in-flight for model: redwood/gaia-13b-8k at 18:02 UTC. overall node CPU fine, GPU util steady but queue depth jumped.

dmitri: linking traces — looks like a burst of long-context embedding requests from customer AcmeAI (client_id: acme-prod). They started a bulk rerun ~18:00.

ben: customer impact? Are API errors happening or just latency?

alice: mostly elevated response latencies. A few 504s from request timeouts when queue exceeded max_inflight. Support reported 2 customers affected (AcmeAI + internal loadtest).

carla: recommended live mitigation options: 1) increase per-node max_inflight temporary 2) enable soft-shedding for low-priority routes 3) throttle AcmeAI by adjusting token quota for the key 4) enable prefix KV cache for embeddings if applicable.

alice: quick proposal: throttle AcmeAI to 60% of baseline, set max_inflight from 120 -> 160 for 10m rolling window, enable soft-shed for non-payg routes. Will coordinate rollback if not helpful. Thoughts?

elaine: +1 to per-customer throttle. We should avoid blanket max_inflight increase if it risks OOM. Check node memory headroom first.

frank: checked mem headroom: avg GPU mem usage at 72%, headroom ~28% on most nodes, a few nodes at 88%. If we raise max_inflight globally we risk filling KV caches. Prefer targeted throttles.

alice: ok doing targeted: applying token_quota throttle for acme-prod_key -> 0.6 of normal. Command: 
```
# runtimectl set-client-quota --client acme-prod_key --ratio 0.6 --reason "live mitigation - bulk rerun" --expires 10m
```
Applying now.

pagerduty-bot: Action logged: set-client-quota by alice at 18:07 UTC (id: act-8851).

dmitri: applying soft-shedding policy for route /v1/embed that marks requests under plan:free as low-priority. This will evict if queue depth > 100 per node.

ben: run command?

dmitri: done: 
```
# runtimectl set-soft-shed --route /v1/embed --priority low --threshold 100 --policy evict-oldest
```
Result: policy deployed to us-west-2 pool at 18:09 UTC.

carla: also toggled timeout tuning to reduce waiting requests surviving the queue: inflight_timeout lowered from 90s -> 45s for low-priority.

alice: summary of live mitigations executed: 1) client quota for AcmeAI -> 60% 2) soft-shed on /v1/embed for free plan (threshold 100) 3) low-priority inflight timeout 45s.

frank: monitoring shows queue p95 dropped from 3.4s -> 1.2s within 90s of mitigations. 504 spikes stopped.

elaine: support: please notify AcmeAI they hit a high-volume rerun and we throttled to preserve cluster stability. Offer options to move to dedicated capacity.

alice: support pinged them in #support-acme. message: "We observed a large bulk job that impacted latency. We applied a temporary throttle and reduced low-priority timeouts to stabilize traffic. If you need steady high throughput consider Redwood Dedicated or staggered jobs."

pagerduty-bot: Incident update: mitigations successful. Continue monitoring for 30m. Incident remains P2 for follow-up (rate-limiting docs + customer opt-in).

dmitri: follow-up tickets: 1) add per-client burst detection to alert earlier (TKT-556) 2) add opt-in auto-scaling policy for clients exceeding X rps (TKT-557) 3) review eviction policy to avoid hot-node saturation (TKT-558).

carla: tldr: avoided global max_inflight bump, used targeted throttles + soft-shed + timeout tuning. Recommend postmortem to capture playbook.

alice: ack — I'll run the postmortem and include heap snapshots + command timeline. If no regressions by 18:40 UTC we'll close. :white_check_mark:

frank: marking incident resolved for live mitigation at 18:32 UTC. Will keep watch for 30m.

pagerduty-bot: Incident resolved (mitigated). Closed at 18:32:10 UTC. Resolution code: mitigation_stable. Logs: act-8851, policy-deploy-3322, timeout-adjust-221.
